note: Declares a plate spec for every vector style, so the depth planes their generators already draw ship as plates instead of being flattened away. No style's art direction changes.
retune_reasons: The vector generators have always drawn named depth groups — the colonnade separates distance, headland, arcade and canopy; the survey plate separates paper, contours and furniture — and the render path flattened them at the moment of render. A consumer wanting parallax had to infer depth from a picture that no longer contained it. These specs stop discarding what the generator already knows.

The alpha is exact, not estimated. Each plate is the whole document with every other plane's marks removed, so a hairline that a segmentation model would smear across two layers stays wholly in its own. That is the property a derived matte cannot have and the reason native plates come before derived ones.

engraved-colonnade-vector draws four planes and this plan caps a stack at three, so its distance plate merges the sea-and-horizon plane with the headland mass. That is an art-direction choice rather than an arithmetic one: both are the far ground and move together, so merging them loses no parallax, where dropping either would lose a layer of the picture. The alternative — enforcing a cap by deleting content — is how a boundary meant to limit scope ends up limiting the work.

survey-relief, pale-moon and tidal-halftone declare three each, matching their generators exactly. Naming fewer would be legal — a style may ship fewer plates than its generator separates — but none of these has an art-direction reason to merge two layers, and a spec that under-declares would quietly lose a layer of parallax for nothing.

Every plate blends normal at full opacity. The generators already compose correctly when flattened, and a blend or opacity here would change what the style looks like — which this version explicitly does not do. Per-plate treatment chains and non-normal blends are art-direction decisions that belong with the work that measures their effect, not with the plumbing that makes them expressible.

The remaining forty styles declare no plate spec and are unchanged. Their raster generators draw one buffer, so a declaration would be a promise nothing can keep: the render path refuses a multi-plate style whose generator does not separate, by name, rather than silently flattening it.

Every style's version is incremented so an install that already holds these rows takes the new value. The seed upserts on id and replaces the row, so a version that does not bump is indistinguishable from one that was never applied.
